'''Grace Awani Alele-Williams ''' {{small|[[Order of the Niger|OON]], FMAN, FNAE}} (16 December 1932 – 25 March 2022) was a Nigerian professor of [[mathematics education]],<ref name="Vanguard20180414">{{Cite news|url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2018/04/grace-alele-williams-mathematician-dealt-cultism-uniben/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Grace Alele-Williams: Mathematician who dealt with cultism at UNIBEN|last=Taire|first=Morenike|date=14 April 2018|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=23 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523011457/https://www.vanguardngr.com/2018/04/grace-alele-williams-mathematician-dealt-cultism-uniben/|url-status=live|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref><ref name="nigeriagalleria">{{Cite web|title=Grace Alele, Role Model, Teacher, Professor, Doctor, Vice-chancellor, Warrior, Prominent Nigerian, Nigeria Personality Profiles|url=https://www.nigeriagalleria.com/Nigeria/Personality-Profiles/Prominent-Nigerians/Grace-Alele.html|access-date=20 May 2021|website=www.nigeriagalleria.com|archive-date=29 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429150337/https://www.nigeriagalleria.com/Nigeria/Personality-Profiles/Prominent-Nigerians/Grace-Alele.html|url-status=live}}</ref> who made history as the first Nigerian woman to receive a [[doctorate]],<ref name="LRiddle-agnesscott.edu">{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Larry |title=Grace Alele Williams |url=https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/williams.htm |website=Biographies of Women Mathematicians |publisher=[[Agnes Scott College]] |access-date=27 March 2022 |date=16 February 2022 |archive-date=22 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222131014/https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/williams.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pulse.ng/communities/student/international-women's-day-5-women-who-have-made-their-marks-in-education/rsw5836|title=5 women who have made their marks in education|date=8 March 2018|newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]|language=en-US|access-date=20 March 2019|archive-date=1 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701120441/https://www.pulse.ng/communities/student/international-womens-day-5-women-who-have-made-their-marks-in-education/rsw5836|url-status=live}}</ref> and the first female [[chancellor (education)|vice-chancellor]] at any [[Nigerian universities|Nigerian university]],<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Quadri |first=Opeyemi |date=30 June 2024 |url=https://edubase.ng/past-present-female-vice-chancellors-in-nigeria-universities/ |access-date=24 August 2024 |website=EdubaseNG}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|date=12 April 2018|title=First Female Vice Chancellor in Nigeria|url=https://hintng.com/first-female-vice-chancellor-in-nigeria/|access-date=27 April 2021|website=Hintnaija|language=en-US|archive-date=27 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427200950/https://hintng.com/first-female-vice-chancellor-in-nigeria/|url-status=live}}</ref>  at the [[University of Benin (Nigeria)|University of Benin]].<ref>{{citation|title=Women Leadership in Nigeria: Stories of Four Women Role Models|author=Nkechi Nwankwo|publisher=Deutchetz Publishers|location=Lagos|year=2006}}. [http://www.sunnewsonline.com/webpages/features/arts/2006/jul/25/arts-25-07-2006-001.htm Review] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120626091727/http://sunnewsonline.com/webpages/features/arts/2006/jul/25/arts-25-07-2006-001.htm |date=26 June 2012 }} by Theresa Onwughalu in the [[Daily Sun]], 25 July 2006.</ref><ref name="AMUCHMA12">{{citation|title=Biographical sketches of famous African mathematicians: Grace Alele Williams|journal=AMUCHMA Newsletter #12|publisher=African Mathematical Union, Commission on the History of Mathematics in Africa|date=27 March 1994|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/AMU/amu_chma_12.html#5|access-date=23 January 2010|archive-date=24 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224215711/http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/AMU/amu_chma_12.html#5|url-status=live}}.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hallmarksoflabour.org/2011/11/prof-mrs-grace-alele-williams-ofr-hlr/ |title=Prof. Mrs Grace Alele Williams OFR, HLR |publisher=Hallmarks of Labour Foundation |date=28 November 2011 |accessdate=9 December 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216151023/http://www.hallmarksoflabour.org/2011/11/prof-mrs-grace-alele-williams-ofr-hlr/ |archivedate=16 December 2013 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Grace Awani Alele was born to [[Itsekiri people|Itsekiri]] parents in [[Warri]], Western Region (present-day [[Delta State]]), [[Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria|Nigeria]] on 16 December 1932.<ref name="Vanguard20220326-Halfmast" /><ref name="GraceAleleWilliamsNoticesAMS">{{Cite journal|last1=Howell|first1=Karin-Therese|last2=Neudauer|first2=Nancy Ann|date=2022|title=Grace Alele-Williams Nigerian Mathematician of Many Firsts - Breaking Down Barriers and Opening Paths|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202203/rnoti-p439.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=69|pages=439–455}}</ref><ref name="Vanguard20220327" /><ref name="MacTutor" /> She attended [[Government School]], Warri, [[Queen's College, Lagos]] and the University College of Ibadan<ref name="silverbirdtv.com">{{Cite web|url=https://silverbirdtv.com/personality-of-the-week-grace-alele-williams-2/|title=Personality of The Week – Grace Alele williams|date=20 November 2014|website=SilverbirdTV|language=en-US|access-date=9 May 2019|archive-date=1 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701120441/https://silverbirdtv.com/personality-of-the-week-grace-alele-williams-2/|url-status=live}}</ref> (now [[University of Ibadan]]). She obtained a [[master's degree]] in mathematics while teaching at [[Queen's School, Ede]] in [[Osun State]] in 1957 and her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in mathematics education at the [[University of Chicago]] ([[United States|U.S.]]) in 1963,<ref name="silverbirdtv.com"/> thereby making her the first Nigerian woman to be awarded a [[doctorate]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grace Alele-Williams – Rest in peace – OMEP |url=https://omepworld.org/grace-alele-williams-rest-in-peace/ |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=omepworld.org}}</ref> Grace Alele was married later that year and became known as Grace Alele-Williams.<ref name="MacTutor" /> She returned to Nigeria for a couple of years' postdoctoral work at the University of Ibadan before joining the [[University of Lagos]] in 1965.<ref name="UBuffalo">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/williams_grace_alele.html|title=Grace Alele Williams - Black Women in Mathematics|website=www.math.buffalo.edu|access-date=9 May 2019|archive-date=4 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304172020/http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/williams_grace_alele.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
Alele-Williams's teaching career started at [[Queen's School, Ibadan|Queen's School, Ede]], [[Osun State]], where she was a mathematics teacher from 1954 to 1957.<ref name="LRiddle-agnesscott.edu" /> She left for the [[University of Vermont]] to become a graduate assistant and later assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rapheal |date=2022-04-08 |title=Grace Alele-Williams (1932-2022) |url=https://thesun.ng/grace-alele-williams-1932-2022/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-01 |newspaper=[[The Sun (Nigeria)|The Sun]]|language=en}}</ref> From 1963 to 1965, Alele-Williams was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral]] research fellow, department (and institute) of education, [[University of Ibadan]] from where she was appointed a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Lagos]] in 1976.<ref name="AMUCHMA12"/>

She had a special interest in women's education.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Odunewu |first=Olusegun |date=2022-03-26 |title=Life, times of Nigeria's first female Vice chancellor, Alele-Williams |url=https://nationaldailyng.com/life-times-of-nigerias-first-female-vice-chancellor-alele-williams/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-01 |newspaper=National Daily|language=en-US}}</ref> While spending a decade directing the institute of education, she introduced innovative non-degree programmes, allowing older women working as elementary school teachers to receive certificates.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Okogba |first=Emmanuel |date=2022-03-26 |title=Grace Alele-Williams dies at 89 |url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/03/grace-alele-williams-dies-at-89/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-10 |newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|language=en-GB}}</ref> Alele-Williams always demonstrated concern for the access of female African students to scientific and technological subjects.<ref name="Vanguard20180414"/> Her interest in mathematics education was originally sparked by her stay in the US, which coincided with the Sputnik phenomenon.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news |last=Jeremiah |first=Urowayino |date=2018-04-14 |title=Grace Alele-Williams: Mathematician who dealt with cultism at UNIBEN |url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2018/04/grace-alele-williams-mathematician-dealt-cultism-uniben/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-01 |newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|language=en-GB}}</ref> Working with the African Mathematics Program in [[Newton, Massachusetts]], under the leadership of MIT professor Ted Martins, she participated in mathematics workshops held in various African cities from 1963 to 1975.<ref name="UBuffalo"/> Highlights included writing texts and correspondence courses covering basic concepts in mathematics working in concert with leading mathematicians and educators,<ref>{{Citation |last=Croom |first=Fred H. |chapter=Covering Spaces |date=1978 |title=Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics |pages=83–104 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4684-9475-4_5 |access-date=2025-02-01 |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-0-387-90288-3}}</ref> such as the book ''Modern Mathematics Handbook for Teachers'' published in 1974.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GRACE ALELE-WILLIAMS: Nigerian Professor and Mathematician |url=https://penglobalinc.com/grace-alele-williams-nigerian-professor-and-mathematician |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=penglobalinc.com |language=en}}</ref> She taught at the University of Lagos from 1965 to 1985, and spent a decade directing the institute of education, which introduced innovative non-degree programmes, with many of the certificate recipients older women working as elementary school teachers.<ref name="AMUCHMA12" /> By serving in various committees and boards, Alele-Williams had made useful contributions in the development of [[education in Nigeria]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=Grace Alele |date=1973-09-01 |title=Education and Government in Northern Nigeria |url=https://doi.org/10.3917/presa.087.0156 |journal=Présence Africaine |volume=87 |issue=3 |pages=156–177 |doi=10.3917/presa.087.0156 |issn=0032-7638|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She was chairman of the [[curriculum]] review committee, former [[Bendel State]] 1973–1979.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grace Alele-Williams|url=https://heelsofinfluence.com/grace-alele-williams/|website=Heels of Influence|language=en-US|access-date=29 May 2020|archive-date=30 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030185853/https://heelsofinfluence.com/grace-alele-williams/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Grace awani ALELE-WILLIAMS – Legacy Way|url=https://www.ourlegacyway.com/grace-awani-alele-williams/|last=admin|date=|website=|language=en-US|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128094639/https://www.ourlegacyway.com/grace-awani-alele-williams/|archive-date=28 November 2020|access-date=2 May 2020}}</ref> From 1979 to 1985, she served as chairman of the [[Lagos State]] curriculum review committee and Lagos State examinations boards.<ref name="UBuffalo"/>

Alele-Williams was appointed vice-chancellor of the University of Benin in 1985, becoming the first female vice-chancellor of a Nigerian university<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1"/> and she believes her appointment, which ended in 1992, was "a test case to demonstrate a woman's executive capability".<ref name="AMUCHMA12"/>

Alele-Williams was a force for reform in the Dark Age for Nigeria's higher education in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oyedibu |first=Enoch |date=2022-04-03 |title=Grace Alele Williams, first Female Vice Chancellor is dead at 89 |url=https://pija.com.ng/just-in-first-female-vice-chancellor-prof-grace-alele-is-dead-at-89/breaking-news/04/2022/ |access-date=2025-02-01 |website=PIJAlance Magazine Limited—The Centre for Public Interest Journalism and Accountability |language=en-GB}}</ref> Then, the activities of secret cults, confraternities and societies had spread within the Nigerian universities, especially in University of Benin.<ref name="auto2"/> She was able to make notable contributions.<ref name="Vanguard20180414" />

After serving as the vice-chancellor of the University of Benin, she joined the board of directors of [[Chevron-Texaco]] Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rapheal |date=2022-04-08 |title=Grace Alele-Williams (1932-2022) |url=https://thesun.ng/grace-alele-williams-1932-2022/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-10 |newspaper=[[The Sun (Nigeria)|The Sun]]|language=en}}</ref> She was also on the board of HIP asset management company limited, an [[asset management company]] in Lagos, Nigeria.<ref name="MacTutor"/>
 
Alele-Williams was a member of governing council, [[UNESCO]] Institute of Education.<ref name="Vanguard20180414"/> She was also a consultant to the UNESCO and Institute of International Education Planning.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Unesco|title=Women in Higher Education Management|url=http://www.unesco.org/education/pdf/24_211.pdf|pages=7|accessdate=13 January 2014|journal=|archive-date=19 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150319022817/http://www.unesco.org/education/pdf/24_211.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="UBuffalo"/> For a decade (1963–73), she was a member of the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences|African Mathematics]] Programme, located in [[Newton, Massachusetts]], United States.<ref name="AMUCHMA12"/> She was vice-president of the World Organisation for Early Childhood Education and later president of the Nigeria chapter,<ref name=":0" /> and the first president of the [[African Mathematical Union]] Commission on Women in Mathematics.<ref name="Ouedraogo Presentation">{{Cite speech| last = Ouedraogo| first = Pr Marie Françoise| author-link = Marie Françoise Ouedraogo| title = AWMA: une association au service des femmes mathématiciennes africaines| event = Femmes et Mathematiques: Mathématiciennes africaines| date = 30 May 2015| location = Institut Henri Poincaré| url = https://femmes-et-maths.fr/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/AWMA-Paris-30-mai-2015.pdf| language = fr| access-date = 15 January 2021| archive-date = 21 January 2021| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210121040402/https://femmes-et-maths.fr/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/AWMA-Paris-30-mai-2015.pdf| url-status = live}}</ref>

She also served ten years (1993–2004) as regional vice-president for Africa of the [[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World|Third World Organization for Women in Science]].<ref name="OWSD">{{cite web |title=Executive Board |url=https://owsd.net/about-owsd/who-we-are/executive-board |website=owsd.net |date=6 February 2015 |publisher=[[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World|OWSD]] |access-date=28 March 2022 |archive-date=20 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620040448/https://owsd.net/about-owsd/who-we-are/executive-board |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
Alele-Williams married Babatunde Abraham Williams (1932–2010) in December 1963, not long after returning to Nigeria from the United States.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ajumobi |first=Kemi |date=2022-03-26 |title=In memoriam: Grace Alele-Williams in five quotes |url=https://businessday.ng/news/article/in-memoriam-grace-alele-williams-in-five-quotes/#google_vignette |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2025-02-01 |newspaper=[[BusinessDay (Nigeria)|BusinessDay]]|language=en-US}}</ref> Williams was a political scientist who, at the time of their marriage, was a senior lecturer at the University of Ife, Osun State.<ref name="MacTutor">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J. J. |last2=Robertson |first2=E. F. |title=Grace Alele-Williams – Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Alele-Williams/ |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |access-date=27 April 2021 |language=en |archive-date=27 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427200950/https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Alele-Williams/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Alele-Williams had five children, and, as of 2017, ten grandchildren.<ref name="nigeriagalleria"/> She died on 25 March 2022 at the age of 89.<ref name="GuardianNG-obit">{{cite news |last1=Egbejule |first1=Michael |title=First female VC, Prof. Grace Alele-Williams, dies at 89 |url=https://guardian.ng/news/first-female-vc-prof-grace-alele-williams-dies-at-89/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=27 March 2022 |date=26 March 2022 |archive-date=27 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327070039/https://guardian.ng/news/first-female-vc-prof-grace-alele-williams-dies-at-89/ |url-status=live |newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Millz |first1=Bayo |date=25 March 2022 |title=Just In: First female VC, Prof Alele-Williams allegedly dies at 89 |url=https://thenewsguru.com/news/just-in-first-female-vc-prof-alele-williams-allegedly-dies-at-89/ |access-date=25 March 2022 |website=TheNewsGuru |language=en-US |archive-date=25 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325183151/https://thenewsguru.com/news/just-in-first-female-vc-prof-alele-williams-allegedly-dies-at-89/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Akintade |first1=Adefemola |date=25 March 2022 |title=Nigeria's first female Vice-Chancellor Grace Alele-Williams is dead |url=https://gazettengr.com/nigerias-first-female-vice-chancellor-grace-alele-williams-is-dead/ |location=Abuja, Nigeria|access-date=25 March 2022 |newspaper=[[Peoples Gazette]]|language=en-US |archive-date=25 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325220825/https://gazettengr.com/nigerias-first-female-vice-chancellor-grace-alele-williams-is-dead/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The next day, the University of Benin flew the institution's flag at [[half-mast]] to mourn her death.<ref name="Vanguard20220326-Halfmast">{{cite news |title=UNIBEN flies flag at half-mast to mourn Alele-Williams |url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/03/uniben-flies-flag-at-half-mast-to-mourn-alele-williams/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=27 March 2022 |date=26 March 2022 |quote=The University of Benin (UNIBEN) on Saturday ordered the flying of the institution’s flag at half-mast to mourn the death of the first female vice-chancellor in Nigeria, Prof. Grace Alele-Williams. Alele-Williams, who was appointed vice-chancellor of the University of Benin in 1985 died on Friday in Lagos at the age of 89 years. ... Prof. Alele-Williams, Nigeria’s first female professor of Mathematics Education was born on Dec. 16, 1932 in Delta to an Itsekiri mother and Owan father from Sobe, Edo. |archive-date=26 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220326193915/https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/03/uniben-flies-flag-at-half-mast-to-mourn-alele-williams/ |url-status=live |newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref><ref name="Vanguard20220327">{{cite news |last1=Ahon |first1=Festus |last2=Ojiego |first2=Nnamdi |last3=Aliu |first3=Ozioruva |title=ALELE – WILLIAMS: More tributes as Okowa, Obaseki mourn |url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/03/alele-williams-more-tributes-as-okowa-obaseki-mourn/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=27 March 2022 |date=27 March 2022 |quote=the UNIBEN have ordered that the institution's flag be mounted at half-mast to mourn the death of the late professor.  Alele-Williams, who passed on Friday evening in Lagos at the age of 89 years, was born in Warri, Delta State. |archive-date=27 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327021846/https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/03/alele-williams-more-tributes-as-okowa-obaseki-mourn/ |url-status=live |newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Alele-Williams received several awards and honours. She received the [[Order of the Niger]] in 1987, and was elected a Fellow of the Mathematical Association of Nigeria and a Fellow of the Nigerian Academy of Education.<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 December 2021 |title=Buhari felicitates first woman Nigerian Professor, Alele-Willaims, at 89 |url=https://thenationonlineng.net/buhari-felicitates-first-woman-nigerian-professor-alele-willaims-at-89/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=7 March 2022 |newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]|language=en-US |archive-date=7 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307113920/https://thenationonlineng.net/buhari-felicitates-first-woman-nigerian-professor-alele-willaims-at-89/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 February 2014, she was one of 100 people to receive the Centenary Award, "a special recognition of unique contributions of Nigerians to the socio-cultural, economic and political development of the country in the last 100 years".<ref>{{Cite news |title=100 Nigerians get Centenary Awards Friday (tonight) [Full List] |url=https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/155979-100-nigerians-get-centenary-awards-friday-tonight-full-list.html |newspaper=[[Premium Times]]|access-date=27 March 2022 |date=28 February 2014 |quote=The full list of the awardees, including those who have rejected the honour is reproduced below along with the categories: ... C. PIONEERS IN PROFESSIONAL CALLINGS/CAREERS ... 30. Professor Grace Alele-Williams |archive-date=27 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327165533/https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/155979-100-nigerians-get-centenary-awards-friday-tonight-full-list.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Akpan |first1=Mike |title=Demeaning Centenary Awards |journal=Realnews Magazine |date=24 March 2014 |url=https://realnewsmagazine.net/news/3079-Demeaning-Centenary-Awards |access-date=27 March 2022 |language=en |archive-date=17 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117101133/https://realnewsmagazine.net/news/3079-Demeaning-Centenary-Awards |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Grace Alele Williams receives deafening ovation|website=Encomium Magazine|url=http://encomium.ng/grace-alele-williams-receives-deafening-ovation/|date=28 February 2014|access-date=27 April 2021|language=en-US|archive-date=27 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427200955/http://encomium.ng/grace-alele-williams-receives-deafening-ovation/|url-status=live}}</ref>

She is included in a deck of playing cards featuring notable women mathematicians published by the Association of Women in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of EvenQuads Deck 1 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#agnesi |url-status=live |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=awm-math.org |archive-date=19 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619004306/https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#alelewilliams }}</ref>
